display.title: Teshuvah, Tefillah and Tzedakah: Getting Ready for the New Year in Elul
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains the three things that earn a good and sweet year in Elul: returning to Hashem, davening more carefully, and giving a little more tzedakah.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, recorded just before Rosh Chodesh Elul. Uncle Yossi reminds children that in Elul Hashem is like a King in the field, close to everyone and ready to inscribe us for a good year, but we must first show that we deserve it. He explains three things. Teshuvah means returning to Hashem: a sin pulls us away, and in Elul we tell Hashem we are sorry and promise to do better. Tefillah means davening more slowly and carefully, because the King is close and listening. Tzedakah means adding a few more coins to the pushka every day. He gives these as the 'order of the month' for every soldier in Tzivos Hashem, and adds a jingle: whatever is good for you is good for your fellow man too, so share these resolutions with friends and family.
display.lesson: In Elul, do teshuvah, daven better and give a little more tzedakah, and help your friends do the same.
